title: Sudan gold miners killed in air strikes near Egypt border, rights group says
title_zh: 苏丹金矿工人遭空袭身亡，人权组织称埃及边境附近发生惨剧
lead: A Sudanese rights group reports that at least 72 civilians prospecting for gold were killed in air strikes on Saturday in River Nile state. Both Egyptian and Sudanese authorities have yet to respond to the allegations.
lead_zh: 苏丹一个人权组织称，周六在尼罗河州发生的空袭导致至少72名淘金平民丧生。埃及和苏丹当局均未对此作出回应。
preview: At least 72 civilians prospecting for gold in Sudan's River Nile state were killed in air strikes on Saturday, according to Emergency Lawyer
preview_zh: 据总部位于喀土穆的人权组织“紧急律师”称，周六在苏丹尼罗河州发生的空袭导致至少72名淘金平民丧生。据称，战机袭击了一个热门矿区的个体采矿者。埃及政府和苏丹事实上的当局均未置评。此前，开罗曾因在打击非法跨境活动中对淘金者发动致命袭击而受到指责。
paragraphs: At least 72 civilians prospecting for gold in Sudan's River Nile state were killed in air strikes on Saturday, according to Emergency Lawyers, a Khartoum-based rights group. The jets allegedly targeted artisanal miners at a popular mining site. Neither the Egyptian government nor Sudan's de facto authorities have commented. Cairo has previously faced accusations of deadly strikes on gold prospectors as part of a crackdown on illicit cross-border activity.

Emergency Lawyers condemned the attack as a violation of Sudan's sovereignty and evidence of the government's tenuous grip on the region. "The deliberate targeting of unarmed civilians violates international humanitarian law and the right to life," it said, adding that the acts may constitute war crimes. The group warned its death toll was provisional and could rise. The Paris-based Sudan Tribune reported that the true toll may far exceed the figure, citing a survivor who said many more were injured.

Eyewitnesses described the assault beginning around 06:00 local time, with aircraft firing more than five missiles directly at the miners' camps, destroying them and excavation pits with people still inside. In June, similar claims emerged that Egyptian forces had used drones and artillery against artisanal mining sites in the same region. Days later, Egypt's border agency launched a sweeping security campaign to combat illegal migration, drug smuggling and illegal mining.

Gold lies at the heart of the border tensions. Sudan's civil war has driven a surge in artisanal mining—a risky practice using rudimentary tools without official permission—particularly in remote border areas. Gold-rich zones like River Nile state lie along porous borders historically associated with smuggling routes. Egypt's border force said in June it had seized 86 tonnes of gold ore and amateur prospecting equipment. Smuggled gold may also fund armed insurgent groups, raising concerns of illicit Sudanese gold undermining Egypt's legitimate market.
paragraphs_zh: 据总部位于喀土穆的人权组织“紧急律师”称，周六在苏丹尼罗河州发生的空袭导致至少72名淘金平民丧生。据称，战机袭击了一个热门矿区的个体采矿者。埃及政府和苏丹事实上的当局均未置评。此前，开罗曾因在打击非法跨境活动中对淘金者发动致命袭击而受到指责。
“紧急律师”谴责此次袭击侵犯了苏丹主权，并表明政府对当地控制薄弱。该组织表示：“故意针对手无寸铁的平民违反国际人道法和生命权”，并补充说这些行为可能构成战争罪。该组织警告称，死亡人数为初步数据，可能进一步上升。总部位于巴黎的《苏丹论坛报》援引一名幸存者的话报道称，实际死亡人数可能远超这一数字，且许多人受伤。
目击者描述，袭击于当地时间早上6点左右开始，飞机向矿工营地直接发射了五枚以上导弹，摧毁了营地和挖掘坑，当时还有人被困在里面。今年6月，曾有类似指控称埃及军队使用无人机和大炮袭击了同一地区的个体采矿点。几天后，埃及边境机构发起了一场大规模安全行动，以打击非法移民、毒品走私和非法采矿。
黄金是边境紧张局势的核心。苏丹内战导致个体采矿激增——这是一种使用简陋工具、未经官方许可的危险做法——尤其是在偏远的边境地区。尼罗河州等黄金资源丰富的地带位于历来与走私路线相关的漏洞百出的边界沿线。埃及边境部队6月表示，已查获86吨金矿石和业余勘探设备。走私黄金还可能为武装叛乱团体提供资金，引发人们对非法苏丹黄金冲击埃及合法市场的担忧。

title_original: Dozens of gold prospectors killed in strikes on Egypt-Sudan border, rights group says
summary_original: Neither Egypt nor Sudan has commented on the alleged strikes on an artisanal mining camp on Saturday.
body_original:
Dozens of gold prospectors killed in strikes on Egypt-Sudan border, rights group says
By
Aleks Phillips
Published
3 hours ago
At least 72 civilians who had been prospecting for gold in a border region of Sudan have been killed in air strikes, a regional rights group says.
Emergency Lawyers, based in the Sudanese capital, Khartoum, said jets targeted the so-called artisanal miners at a popular gold mining sites in Sudan's River Nile state on Saturday.
Neither the Egyptian government nor the de facto Sudanese authorities have so far commented.
Cairo has previously faced accusations of deadly strikes on gold prospectors as part of a crackdown on illicit activity along its southern border.
Emergency Lawyers noted the previous alleged attacks and said they represented not only a violation of Sudan's sovereign territory but demonstrated the government's lack of control over the region.
"The deliberate targeting of unarmed civilians violates international humanitarian law and the right to life," it said in a statement on Sunday. "These acts may constitute war crimes."
It noted that its death toll was provisional and could rise.
The Paris-based Sudan Tribune reported that the death toll could far exceed the number reported by Emergency Lawyers, citing a survivor of Saturday's attack who said many more people had been injured.
Eyewitnesses said the attack began around 06:00 local time (04:00 GMT), with the aircraft firing more than five missiles directly at the miners' camps, destroying them and excavation pits with people still inside, the newspaper wrote.
The Sudan Tribune reported claims in June that Egyptian forces had used drones and artillery to target artisanal mining sites in the same region, killing several, after sporadic incidents of Egyptian border guards of burning equipment, torching temporary shelters, and firing live ammunition to disperse mine workers.
Days later, Egypt's border agency announced that it and the military had begun a sweeping security campaign along the border to foil illegal migration, drug smuggling and illegal mining.
At the same time, Sudan's de facto leader announced an investigation into the alleged strikes, which were said to have killed dozens.
Gold lies at the core of the border tensions.
Sudan's ongoing civil war has led to a surge in artisanal mining - an often risky practice conducted by civilians with rudimentary tools and without official permission - particularly in remote areas near its borders.
Gold-rich areas such as those in River Nile state lie along porous borders in terrain historically associated with cross-border smuggling routes, with artisanally mined gold potentially feeding into those channels.
Egypt's border force said in June that it had seized 86 tonnes of gold ore along with amateur prospecting equipment.
Artisanal mining has also reportedly continued in Sudan's conflict zones and smuggled gold may be a source of income for armed insurgent groups.
This has raised concerns of illicit Sudanese gold undermining the legitimate Egyptian gold market.
